references.text: In the preceding verse ([ref:Luk 22:67|Luke 22:67]), they ask Jesus to say whether he is the Christ, and he answers that even if he tells them, they will not believe. Verse 68 continues this line of thought: even if he asks them questions, they will not answer.

In [ref:Jer 38:15|Jeremiah 38:15], Jeremiah says to King Zedekiah: "If I give you advice, you will not listen to me." The same pattern appears here: the one speaking God's word knows that the other party will neither believe nor answer honestly.

In [ref:Joh 3:12|John 3:12], Jesus says: "When I have spoken to you about earthly things and you do not believe, how can you believe if I speak to you about heavenly things?" Jesus points out that his listeners will not respond to what he says, no matter what he tells them.

In [ref:Joh 8:45-47|John 8:45-47], Jesus says that because he speaks the truth, they do not believe him, and that whoever is from God hears God's word. The religious leaders refused to believe and answer, which reflects Jesus' words in Luke 22:68.

In [ref:Luk 20:3-7|Luke 20:3-7], Jesus asks a counter-question about John's baptism, and the religious leaders refuse to answer because they fear the consequences. This is a concrete example of what Jesus describes in 22:68 – that they will not answer when he asks them.

In [ref:Matt 21:23-27|Matthew 21:23-27], the chief priests and elders refuse to answer Jesus' question about John's baptism. This parallels the event in Luke 20 and shows the pattern Jesus refers to in Luke 22:68.

In [ref:Jes 6:9-10|Isaiah 6:9-10], it is prophesied about a people who hear but do not understand, and see but do not perceive. This spiritual hardening lies behind the attitude Jesus meets in Luke 22:68 – the religious leaders would neither believe his answer nor respond to his question.
